# Firefly Banking Platform — Claude Code Skills

Claude Code skills for accelerating development on the **Firefly Banking Platform** — core banking, lending, payments, customer management, and enterprise integrations.

> These skills target experienced developers working with the [Firefly Banking Platform](https://github.com/firefly-oss) (`com.firefly.*`). You should also install the [Firefly Framework skills](https://github.com/fireflyframework/fireflyframework-claude-skills) for foundational patterns (CQRS, Sagas, EDA, R2DBC).

## Installation

```bash
# 1. Install framework skills first (foundation)
/plugin marketplace add fireflyframework/fireflyframework-claude-skills
/plugin install fireflyframework-claude-skills@fireflyframework-skills

# 2. Install banking skills
/plugin marketplace add firefly-oss/firefly-oss-claude-skills
/plugin install firefly-oss-claude-skills@firefly-oss-skills
```

**Important:** Install both plugins. Banking skills build on framework skills. The framework plugin provides CQRS, Sagas, EDA, R2DBC, caching, resilience, and observability patterns. The banking plugin adds domain-specific guidance for payments, lending, compliance, and integrations.

After installation, skills activate automatically based on context. Commands are invoked with `/command-name`.

---

## How Skills Work

This plugin provides three types of Claude Code extensions. Understanding when and how each type activates is key to getting the most out of them.

### Skills (Context-Sensitive)

Skills activate **automatically** when Claude Code detects you're working on a relevant banking task. You don't need to invoke them — just describe what you want to do.

**How they activate:** Claude Code reads your prompt and the surrounding code context. When it recognizes a banking-domain pattern (e.g., "implement a payment flow", "add KYC verification", "create a loan product"), it loads the relevant skill and uses its guidance to produce platform-correct code.

**What they contain:** Each skill is a detailed reference document with real API classes, DTOs, annotations, service interactions, and configuration from the actual Firefly Banking Platform source code. They reference `com.firefly.*` classes, real saga steps, actual PSP/rail adapter interfaces, and production-grade patterns.

**When multiple skills apply:** Skills chain naturally. For example, asking "add a payment flow with PSD2 compliance and webhook notifications" activates `implement-payment-flow` + `implement-psd-openbanking` + `implement-webhook-callback`. Claude Code merges their guidance to produce code that correctly integrates all three concerns.

### Commands (Slash-Invoked)

Commands are **explicitly invoked** with a slash prefix and generate banking-specific code scaffolds.

**How they work:** Type `/command-name <args>` in your Claude Code prompt. The command generates a full file tree with correct `firefly-parent` POM inheritance, `firefly-bom` imports, banking package naming (`com.firefly.*`), Spring Cloud Config, and SDK registration.

**When to use them:** Use commands at the start of new work — a new banking module, a new PSP adapter, a new lending product. They ensure the foundational structure matches the ~55-repo ecosystem conventions.

### Agents (Specialized Reviewers)

Agents are **invoked by Claude Code** when it determines your task benefits from specialized banking review or architectural guidance. You can also request them explicitly.

**How they work:** Agents have deep banking domain knowledge — double-entry accounting, PCI-DSS, PSD2/GDPR/AML regulations, saga compensation, inter-service communication rules, and multi-tenancy isolation. They produce severity-tiered findings (CRITICAL/WARNING/INFO).

**When to use them:**
- **`banking-domain-reviewer`** — After implementing a feature: *"Review this payment handler for compliance and accounting correctness"*
- **`banking-architect`** — Before starting a feature: *"Help me decide where to put this new escrow feature in the ecosystem"*

## Skills Catalog (25)

### Scaffolding & Domain Conventions

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`banking-domain-conventions`** | Writing any code in a firefly-oss service. Covers service taxonomy (core-banking/core-lending/core-common/core-data/domain-\*/exp-\*/app-\*), `com.firefly.*` package naming, POM inheritance (`firefly-parent` -> `fireflyframework-parent`), BOM imports, module structure, and inter-service communication rules. |
| **`create-banking-service`** | Creating a new banking microservice. Extends framework scaffolding with `firefly-parent` inheritance, `firefly-bom` imports, Spring Cloud Config client, SDK registration, and domain-specific patterns. |
| **`generate-execution-plan`** | Transforming a high-level work plan into a step-by-step execution document. Generates self-contained Claude Code prompts that follow bottom-up build order (core → SDK → domain → experience/app), protect the stable core layer, stub third-party integrations, and include verification gates between phases. |

### Core Banking

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`implement-payment-flow`** | Implementing payment features. Covers `PspAdapter` (Stripe, Adyen, PayPal — 9 ports), `RailAdapter` (SEPA, ACH, SWIFT — 16 rail types), `ResilientPspService`, double-entry accounting via `TransactionDTO`/`TransactionLegDTO`, and payment order orchestration. |
| **`implement-account-operations`** | Working with accounts or ledger. Covers account opening, movements, double-entry transactions, standing orders, account spaces, multi-currency, GL journal posting, restrictions, interest operations, and statements. |
| **`implement-psd-openbanking`** | Implementing PSD2/PSD3/FIDA features. Covers consent lifecycle, SCA integration, Account Information Service (AIS), Payment Initiation Service (PIS), TPP management, access logging, and PSDx security architecture. |

### Core Lending

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`implement-lending-workflow`** | Implementing loan workflows. Covers end-to-end origination saga (`RegisterApplicationSaga`), credit scoring, underwriting, disbursement, servicing, and provisioning. Maps all domain-lending-\* -> core-lending-\* service interactions. |
| **`implement-collections-delinquency`** | Implementing delinquency management. Covers delinquency tracking, collection cases, actions, promises, escalations, status history, and IFRS 9 provisioning integration with staging. |
| **`implement-credit-product`** | Creating new credit product types. Covers product catalog configuration for personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, asset finance, and supply chain finance with origination, scoring, and servicing integration. Also covers credit card operations: revolving lines, billing cycles, statements, and payment processing via `core-lending-credit-cards`. |
| **`implement-asset-finance`** | Implementing renting and leasing products. Covers asset lifecycle tracking, delivery and pickup logistics, residual value management, and integration with loan servicing via `core-lending-asset-finance`. |
| **`implement-regulatory-compliance`** | Implementing lending regulatory compliance features. Covers AML case management, SAR processing, regulatory reporting (CIRBE, FINREP, COREP, SEPBLAC), compliance workflows, and sanctions screening via `core-lending-regulatory-compliance`. |

### Core Common (Shared Services)

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`implement-customer-lifecycle`** | Working with customer management. Covers the 14-step `RegisterCustomerSaga`, Party/NaturalPerson/LegalEntity model, KYC/KYB flows, SCA integration, GDPR compliance, PEP tracking, and domain events. |
| **`implement-product-catalog`** | Managing financial products. Covers product lifecycle (DRAFT -> ACTIVE -> RETIRED), `RegisterProductSaga` (19 steps), versioning, configuration types, eligibility rules, and distributor assignment. |
| **`implement-contract-management`** | Working with contracts. Covers contract lifecycle (7 states), party assignment, dynamic term templates (11 categories), document attachment, e-signature integration, event history, and risk assessments. |
| **`implement-modelhub-entities`** | Creating dynamic entities (no-code). Covers ModelHub metadata-driven entities with JSONB storage, field types, validation, structured querying, and schema evolution — no deployment needed. |
| **`implement-config-management`** | Multi-tenant configuration management. Covers provider settings, channel configuration, feature flags with gradual rollout, credential vault integration, environment-scoped config, and webhook management via `core-common-config-mgmt`. |
| **`implement-distributor-management`** | Distributor lifecycle management. Covers distributor onboarding, multi-tier hierarchies, region management, agreements, commission structures, and branding configuration via `core-common-distributor-mgmt`. |

### Enterprise Integrations

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`implement-idp-integration`** | Integrating identity providers. Covers the `IdpAdapter` port with Keycloak, Cognito, Azure AD (B2C/Entra), and Internal DB adapters. Shows `app-authenticator` wiring and configuration per provider. |
| **`implement-ecm-integration`** | Document management or e-signatures. Covers `DocumentPort`/`DocumentContentPort` for S3/Azure Blob storage, `SignatureEnvelopePort` for DocuSign/Logalty, `@EcmAdapter` annotation, and resilience patterns. |
| **`implement-notification-flow`** | Sending notifications. Covers `EmailProvider` (SendGrid/Resend), `SMSProvider` (Twilio), `PushProvider` (Firebase), template management, user preferences, and audit trail. |
| **`implement-webhook-callback`** | Inbound webhooks or outbound callbacks. Covers `WebhookProcessor` for receiving, `CallbackDispatcherImpl` for sending, HMAC signature validation, retry policies, circuit breakers, and DLQ. |

### Backoffice & Configuration

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`implement-backoffice-feature`** | Adding backoffice functionality. Covers `AbstractBackofficeController`/`AbstractBackofficeResourceController`, context resolution, permissions, user/org management, and audit trail. |
| **`implement-multi-tenancy`** | Multi-tenant isolation. Covers `ExecutionContext.tenantId`, `TenantContext` in Reactor chains, row-level data partitioning, per-tenant configuration, and distributor branding. |

### Testing

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| **`testing-banking-flows`** | Writing integration tests for banking flows. Covers payment flow testing with mocked PSPs/rails, loan origination saga tests, customer onboarding with KYC mocks, and banking test data builders. |
| **`testing-regulatory-compliance`** | Testing compliance requirements. Covers PSD2 consent validation, SCA enforcement, AML/KYC verification, regulatory reporting, audit trail verification, and GDPR data handling tests. |

## Usage Guide

### Skill Activation & Chaining

Skills activate based on the **intent** in your prompt and the banking domain context. Here are the key patterns:

| What you say | Skills that activate |
|--------------|---------------------|
| "Create a payment order with Stripe" | `implement-payment-flow` |
| "Open a new savings account" | `implement-account-operations` |
| "Add PSD2 consent to this endpoint" | `implement-psd-openbanking` |
| "Implement the loan origination saga" | `implement-lending-workflow` |
| "Add delinquency tracking for overdue loans" | `implement-collections-delinquency` |
| "Configure a new mortgage product" | `implement-credit-product` |
| "Add a step to the customer registration saga" | `implement-customer-lifecycle` |
| "Manage product lifecycle states" | `implement-product-catalog` |
| "Add e-signature to the contract flow" | `implement-contract-management` + `implement-ecm-integration` |

| "Integrate Keycloak for authentication" | `implement-idp-integration` |
| "Send an email notification on payment success" | `implement-notification-flow` |
| "Handle Stripe webhooks" | `implement-webhook-callback` |
| "Add a backoffice screen for loan approvals" | `implement-backoffice-feature` |
| "Isolate data by tenant" | `implement-multi-tenancy` |
| "Configure a provider for a tenant" | `implement-config-management` |
| "Add a feature flag with gradual rollout" | `implement-config-management` |
| "Onboard a new distributor with regions" | `implement-distributor-management` |
| "Implement renting/leasing for equipment" | `implement-asset-finance` |

**Chaining examples:**
- "Process a SEPA payment with PSD2 consent and send a notification" → `implement-payment-flow` + `implement-psd-openbanking` + `implement-notification-flow`
- "Add a backoffice loan approval screen with tenant isolation" → `implement-backoffice-feature` + `implement-multi-tenancy` + `implement-lending-workflow`

### Using Commands Effectively

Commands generate the scaffolding; skills guide the implementation. Use commands **first**, then describe what you want to build:

```
# 1. Create a new core-banking module for escrow accounts
/create-banking-module banking escrow-accounts

# 2. Then describe the feature
> Implement account opening for escrow accounts with hold and release operations,
> double-entry ledger posting, and GL journal entries.

# Skills implement-account-operations and implement-payment-flow activate
# to guide the implementation with correct DTOs and patterns.
```

```
# 1. Create a PSP adapter for Square
/create-payment-adapter square

# 2. Then implement the ports
> Implement the PaymentPort and RefundPort for Square's API.
> Use ResilientPspService for all external calls.

# Skill implement-payment-flow activates to guide the port implementation.
```

```
# 1. Create a new asset finance product
/create-lending-product asset-finance

# 2. Then customize
> Add equipment depreciation tracking and residual value calculation
> to the asset finance servicing flow.

# Skill implement-credit-product activates for the customization.
```

### Working with Agents

**Banking Domain Reviewer** — catches banking-specific issues that a generic code review would miss:

```
> Review my payment handler implementation

banking-domain-reviewer checks:
  - Double-entry accounting: Do transaction legs balance? (CRITICAL)
  - PCI-DSS: Are card numbers masked? No raw PAN in logs? (CRITICAL)
  - Saga compensation: Does every creation step have a compensate method? (CRITICAL)
  - AML compliance: Is PaymentComplianceManagerService called before execution? (WARNING)
  - Domain naming: Does the package follow com.firefly.core.banking.* conventions? (INFO)
  - Inter-service rules: Core services don't call other core services? (WARNING)
  - Multi-tenancy: Is tenantId propagated in ExecutionContext? (WARNING)
```

**Banking Architect** — provides ecosystem-aware architectural guidance:

```
> I need to build a feature for recurring payments with dynamic scheduling.
> Where does this go?

banking-architect analyzes:
  - Tier placement: Domain-tier (orchestrates core-banking-payments + core-banking-accounts)
  - Service: Extend domain-payment-scheduling or create new
  - Saga design: RecurringPaymentSaga with schedule evaluation + payment execution steps
  - Integration: SDK to core-banking-payments, Kafka events for schedule triggers
  - Data: No owned tables (domain tier), schedule config in core-banking-payments
  - Compliance: SCA for initial setup, no SCA for scheduled executions (PSD2 exemption)
```

### Combining Skills, Commands, and Agents

The typical workflow for a new banking feature:

```
1. ASK THE ARCHITECT     → "Where should recurring payments go in the ecosystem?"
                           Architect recommends: domain-tier, extend or create domain-payment-scheduling

2. SCAFFOLD              → /create-banking-module banking payment-scheduling
                           (or use existing service if extending)

3. DESIGN THE SAGA       → "Create a saga for recurring payment execution"
                           implement-lending-workflow / implement-payment-flow activate

4. IMPLEMENT PAYMENTS    → "Execute the payment via the configured PSP/rail"
                           implement-payment-flow activates with PspAdapter/RailAdapter guidance

5. ADD COMPLIANCE        → "Add PSD2 consent validation for the initial setup"
                           implement-psd-openbanking activates

6. ADD NOTIFICATIONS     → "Send email confirmation on each recurring payment"
                           implement-notification-flow activates

7. WRITE TESTS           → "Test the recurring payment saga end-to-end"
                           testing-banking-flows activates

8. COMPLIANCE TESTS      → "Test PSD2 consent and SCA for the setup flow"
                           testing-regulatory-compliance activates

9. REVIEW                → "Review all changes with the banking domain reviewer"
                           banking-domain-reviewer scans for accounting, compliance, naming issues
```

Banking skills build on top of framework skills. Here's how they relate:

| `implement-payment-flow` | `implement-cqrs` (handlers), `implement-resilience` (PSP calls) |

| `implement-customer-lifecycle` | `implement-saga` (registration saga), `implement-reactive-r2dbc` (entities) |
| `implement-account-operations` | `implement-cqrs` (account commands/queries), `implement-reactive-r2dbc` (ledger) |
| `implement-idp-integration` | `implement-hexagonal-adapter` (IdpAdapter port/adapter) |

## Practical Examples

### Example 1: Creating a New Lending Product (End-to-End)

**Scenario:** The business wants to offer **equipment leasing** as a new credit product.

**Step 1: Ask the architect**

```
> We want to add equipment leasing as a new lending product. Where does this
> fit in the ecosystem and what services are involved?
```

The `banking-architect` agent maps out:
- **Product definition** → `core-common-product-mgmt` (new product type)
- **Origination** → `domain-lending-loan-origination` (saga extension)
- **Credit scoring** → `core-lending-credit-scoring` (equipment-specific model)
- **Servicing** → `core-lending-loan-servicing` (lease payments, residual value)
- **Collateral** → `core-lending-collateral-management` (equipment as collateral)

**Step 2: Scaffold the product**

```
/create-lending-product asset-finance
```

This generates product catalog configuration, origination saga extensions, and servicing mappings for the asset-finance product type.

**Step 3: Configure the product catalog entry**

```
> Create the product catalog configuration for equipment leasing with
> term ranges 12-60 months, max amount 500K, and equipment depreciation.
```

The `implement-product-catalog` skill activates and generates the `RegisterProductSaga` extension with the correct 19-step flow, plus eligibility rules and configuration types.

**Step 4: Extend the origination saga**

```
> Add an equipment valuation step to the origination saga that runs
> after credit scoring but before underwriting
```

The `implement-lending-workflow` skill activates and shows how to add a new `@SagaStep` to `RegisterApplicationSaga` with proper `dependsOn` ordering and compensation.

**Step 5: Add collateral tracking**

```
> Register the leased equipment as collateral in core-lending-collateral-management
```

**Step 6: Test the full flow**

```
> Write integration tests for the equipment leasing origination flow,
> including credit scoring mocks and collateral registration
```

`testing-banking-flows` activates with loan origination saga test patterns, mocked credit bureau calls, and banking test data builders.

**Step 7: Review**

```
> Review the equipment leasing implementation with the banking domain reviewer
```

---

### Example 2: Adding a New Payment Service Provider (PSP) Adapter

**Scenario:** You need to integrate **Square** as a new PSP for card payments.

**Step 1: Scaffold the adapter**

```
/create-payment-adapter square
```

This generates the complete adapter structure in `library-psps/`:

```
library-psps/src/main/java/com/firefly/psps/square/
  SquarePspAdapter.java              # Main adapter (9 ports)
  SquarePspService.java              # Service with ResilientPspService
  config/
    SquareConfiguration.java         # Circuit breaker, rate limiter beans
    SquareProperties.java            # API keys, base URL, sandbox mode
  ports/
    SquarePaymentPort.java           # PaymentPort implementation (7 methods)
    SquareRefundPort.java            # RefundPort implementation
    SquarePayoutPort.java            # PayoutPort implementation
    SquareCustomerPort.java          # CustomerPort implementation
    SquareDisputePort.java           # DisputePort implementation
    SquareSubscriptionPort.java      # SubscriptionPort implementation
    SquareCheckoutPort.java          # CheckoutPort implementation
    SquareReconciliationPort.java    # ReconciliationPort implementation
    SquareProviderSpecificPort.java  # Provider-specific operations
```

**Step 2: Implement the payment port**

```
> Implement the SquarePaymentPort using Square's Java SDK.
> Map CreatePaymentRequest -> Square's CreatePaymentRequest and back.
```

The `implement-payment-flow` skill activates and guides:
- Request/response mapping to/from `PaymentResponse`
- Wrapping calls with `ResilientPspService.execute()`
- Never storing raw card data (PCI-DSS)
- Using `ComplianceService.maskSensitiveData()` for logging

**Step 3: Handle webhooks**

```
> Add webhook handling for Square payment status updates
```

The `implement-webhook-callback` skill activates with HMAC signature validation, `WebhookProcessor` registration, and DLQ configuration for failed processing.

**Step 4: Add ledger integration**

```
> Post the Square payment to the ledger with balanced debit/credit legs
> and GL journal entries
```

The `implement-payment-flow` skill shows the 3-record coordination:
1. `TransactionDTO` + `TransactionLegDTO` (DEBIT/CREDIT) in `core-banking-ledger`
2. `AccountBalanceDTO` update in `core-banking-accounts`
3. `JournalBatchDTO` + `JournalEntryDTO` in `core-common-accounting-gl`

**Step 5: Test**

```
> Write tests for the Square adapter with mocked Square API responses
```

`testing-banking-flows` provides PSP testing patterns with WireMock stubs for the Square API.

### Example 3: Building a Customer Onboarding Extension

**Scenario:** You need to add **video KYC verification** as a new step in the customer registration saga.

**Step 1: Understand the current saga**

```
> Show me the current RegisterCustomerSaga steps and where video KYC
> should fit in
```

The `implement-customer-lifecycle` skill activates and shows all 14 steps of `RegisterCustomerSaga`, including the dependency DAG. Video KYC would slot after `createNaturalPerson` and before `assignRiskProfile`.

**Step 2: Add the saga step**

```
> Add a videoKycVerification step to RegisterCustomerSaga that calls
> a video KYC provider and stores the verification result
```

The skill generates:

```java
@SagaStep(id = "videoKycVerification", compensate = "revokeVideoKyc",
          dependsOn = "createNaturalPerson")
@StepEvent(type = "customer.videokyc.completed")
public Mono<UUID> videoKycVerification(VideoKycCommand cmd, SagaContext ctx) {
    UUID partyId = ctx.getVariableAs("partyId", UUID.class);
    return cmd == null ? Mono.empty()
        : commandBus.send(cmd.withPartyId(partyId));
}

public Mono<Void> revokeVideoKyc(UUID verificationId, SagaContext ctx) {
    return verificationId == null ? Mono.empty()
        : commandBus.send(new RevokeVideoKycCommand(
            ctx.getVariableAs("partyId", UUID.class), verificationId));
}
```

**Step 3: Create the hexagonal adapter for the video KYC provider**

```
> Create a hexagonal adapter for the video KYC provider following
> the same pattern as the IDP adapters
```

The `implement-idp-integration` skill (as a reference pattern) plus `implement-hexagonal-adapter` (from the framework plugin) guide the port/adapter creation with `@ConditionalOnProperty` for provider selection.

**Step 4: Add GDPR compliance**


### Example 4: Implementing Open Banking (PSD2) Endpoints

**Scenario:** You need to expose Account Information Service (AIS) endpoints for third-party providers.

### Example 5: Creating a New Domain-Tier Orchestration Service

**Scenario:** You need to build `domain-trade-finance` that orchestrates letter of credit issuance across `core-banking-payments`, `core-banking-accounts`, `core-common-customer-mgmt`, and `core-lending-collateral-management`.

## Service Ecosystem (~55 Repos)

Understanding where your code fits in the ecosystem is critical. The `banking-architect` agent and `banking-domain-conventions` skill help with placement, but here's a reference:

| Domain | Core Services (own data) | Domain Services (orchestrate) | Experience Services (BFF) | App Services (infra edge) |
|--------|-------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Banking** | `core-banking-accounts`, `core-banking-ledger`, `core-banking-payments`, `core-banking-cards`, `core-banking-psdx` | — | `exp-payments` | — |
| **Lending** | `core-lending-loan-origination`, `core-lending-credit-scoring`, `core-lending-loan-servicing`, `core-lending-provisioning-risk`, `core-lending-collateral-management`, `core-lending-mortgage`, `core-lending-credit-cards`, `core-lending-asset-finance`, `core-lending-regulatory-compliance` | `domain-lending-loan-origination` | `exp-lending` | — |
| **Common** | `core-common-customer-mgmt`, `core-common-kycb-mgmt`, `core-common-sca-mgmt`, `core-common-product-mgmt`, `core-common-org-mgmt`, `core-common-user-mgmt`, `core-common-security-vault`, `core-common-accounting-gl`, `core-common-reference-master-data`, `core-common-config-mgmt`, `core-common-distributor-mgmt`, `core-common-document-mgmt` | `domain-customer-people`, `domain-customer-kyc-kyb`, `domain-product-catalog`, `domain-distributor-branding`, `domain-core-security-center` | `exp-onboarding`, `exp-profile` | `app-authenticator`, `app-configurator-masters` |
| **Data** | `core-data-credit-bureaus`, `core-data-template` | — | — | — |
| **Libraries** | `library-psps`, `library-rails`, `library-common-*`, `library-utils`, `library-workflow-engine`, `library-plugin-manager-*` | — | — | — |

**Key rules:**
- **Core → Core calls are NOT allowed.** Core services are self-contained.
- **Domain → Core via SDK** (sync WebClient). Standard pattern.
- **Domain → Domain via Kafka events** (async). For long-running cross-domain workflows.
- **Experience → Domain via SDK** (sync WebClient). Experience services consume only domain SDKs, never core directly.
- **App → Domain via SDK** (sync WebClient). Standard pattern.
- **Dependency direction**: `channel → exp-* → domain-* → core-*` and `app-* → domain-* → core-*`. Never invert.
